cheapStock.name: Cheap-stock call near the price
cheapStock.evidence: claudebot-cheapstock-calls-research.json (real historical option prices, Feb 2024 on): the call within 3% of the price, 30 days out, on names at $25 or less made money in both periods: 2024 23 trades, 57% wins, +15.2% average; unseen 2025-26 30 trades, 57% wins, +13.7% average; with a wide buy/sell gap (4 cents or 8%) +6.6% and +6.8%. expectedRetPct is the lower wide-gap figure. THIN: 53 trades on nine names, five trades made two-thirds of the profit, earnings were not skipped in the test, 2026 was about flat. Calls further from the price lost in both periods. No paper trades yet.

boardApproval.by: board, 2026-11-11: asked whether to skip the 30-paper-trade rule and trade these with real money, chose 'Live: cheap-stock + index'
boardApproval.terms: one option at a time, up to $50 (about 43% of the account); a losing trade can lose the whole premium; earnings skipped; the rule switches itself off after 10 live trades if it is losing

cheapStock.boardReenabled: 2026-11-11 13:01 CT: board, after being shown that the rule lost on the 66 added stocks in both periods: 'No run it'.

index.name: Index-fund $50 call
index.evidence: claudebot-dipcall-cheap-research.json (real historical option prices): the closest-to-the-price call costing $50 or less, 45 days out, on SPY, QQQ and IWM: 2024 18 trades, 50% wins, +2.5% average; unseen 2025-26 23 trades, 61% wins, +15.4% average. expectedRetPct is the lower (2024) figure, so a quote even one cent wider than the test assumed usually fails the forecast and is skipped. WEAKER THAN cheapStock: the index-only cut was chosen after seeing the all-funds result (which lost in 2024), samples are small, and the contract sits about 9 to 11% above the price. No paper trades yet.

evidence: LIVE by board order 2026-11-11 for two rules only (see rules.*.evidence for each rule's numbers and limits). The desk's earlier rule (+10% target, -40% stop on cheap out-of-the-money calls) lost in both periods and is retired. The hard caps in claudebot/governor.py are unchanged.
changeLog: 2026-11-02: Board ordered a live options-buying desk that takes profit right away. CEO built it on the Dip signal with a +10% resting take-profit, -40% stop, 7-day limit, max 25% of account ($30) per option, one at a time.
2026-11-02: Board raised the per-option cap to $50 / 43% of account (was $30 / 25%) so the desk can act on Dip signals; audit ceiling raised to $50 / 45% to match.

2026-11-02: Board ordered options on any stock. CEO added a nightly scan of ~110 liquid optionable stocks/ETFs (price $5-150); the hourly run fetches live quotes only for names near their dip trigger. Tested ETFs first, then the deepest dips; stocks skip earnings within 10 days. Caps unchanged ($50 / 43%, one option at a time).
2026-11-02: Board chose to focus on the tested Dip desk: options-buying desk switched off for new entries (the option part was never backtested). Any held option is still managed to its exit.

2026-11-11: Board order ('Live: cheap-stock + index', chosen when asked whether to skip the 30-paper-trade rule). Desk switched ON for two rules: (1) cheap-stock call within 3% of the price, about 30 days out, on scan-list names at $25 or less; (2) the closest-to-the-price $50 call about 45 days out on SPY, QQQ, IWM. Exit now follows the stock, as tested (5% stock stop, back above its 5-day average near the close, 10 days), with no resting take-profit and no premium stop. Earnings buffer widened from 10 to 14 days to cover the holding window. Caps unchanged ($50 / 43%, one option at a time). Each rule switches itself off after 10 closed live trades with profit factor below 1.0. Evidence is thin and there are no paper trades; the paper desks for both ideas keep running.

2026-11-11: Board order ('Widen it'): 66 more stocks added to scanUniverse, all priced about $5 to $26.50 on 2026-11-11, so the cheap-stock call rule sees more dip signals. Same rule, caps and checks; contracts with wide or thin quotes are still skipped by the planner. These names were not in the research that supported the rule; a rerun of that research on the wider list is reported separately.

2026-11-11: Board order ('Make sure it watches all stocks'): the nightly scan now also discovers every active US stock with listed options, keeps those priced $5 to about $26.50 with enough trading, and computes their dip triggers, so the cheap-stock call rule watches the whole market, not only scanUniverse. Same rule, caps and quote checks.

2026-11-11: Board order ('Buy and sell throughout the day not just a certain time'): the options desk now buys at any run from 8:40 to 2:59 CT on a live dip signal, and sells at any run once the stock is back above its 5-day average or day 10 is reached (the 5% stock stop already applied at any run). The research bought and sold at the close, so intraday entries and exits are untested for this desk; the Dip desk's own all-day test (2026-11-06) found all-day buys about 12% less profitable in total than near-close buys but still positive. GitHub's 5-minute gate now checks the options signals on live prices and calls the trader when one appears.
2026-11-11: CEO paused the cheap-stock call rule (risk reduction) after the rerun on new stocks failed in both periods; the index rule is unchanged. Waiting for the board.
2026-11-11: Board re-enabled the cheap-stock call rule across the whole market ('No run it') after seeing the failed rerun. Caps, quote checks and the 10-trade self switch-off unchanged.
